item.research_question: How does chemical short-range order (SRO) affect the plastic response, dislocation mobility, and defect evolution during nanoindentation in the bcc HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy compared to a random alloy and an elementary Ta crystal?
item.material_system: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr (Senkov alloy) in random and short-range-ordered (SRO) states; pure Ta crystal
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics simulations using LAMMPS; SRO created via Monte Carlo simulation at 100 K (4.7×10^6 steps); nanoindentation with a repulsive sphere (R=10 nm) at 20 m/s to 4 nm depth, held for 100 ps, then retracted at 20 m/s; temperature maintained at 10 mK
item.test_conditions: Constant time step of 1 fs; bottom and lateral sides fixed; thermostat at 10 mK; indenter stiffness k=3.3 eV/Å^3; final depth d=4 nm reached at t=200 ps
key_findings: The SRO alloy is 10% harder than the random HEA (H_ind increased by 10%).
The SRO alloy exhibits the highest dislocation density, remaining constant at 1.6–1.8×10^16 m^-2 throughout all phases.
The plastic zone in the SRO alloy extends farthest, with 78% of dislocations surviving retraction compared to negligible survival in Ta.
Elemental Ta shows abundant prismatic dislocation loop emission via the lasso mechanism, which is suppressed in both alloys.
The SRO alloy features zero twinning volume, whereas Ta and the random HEA show significant twinning that partially survives retraction.
The reduction in hold hardness is least for the SRO alloy (20%) compared to the elementary crystal (27%), indicating enhanced difficulty of stress relaxation.
Dislocation segment length is shortest in SRO (4.1 nm) compared to random HEA (4.7 nm) and Ta (5.8 nm).
item.mechanism: The slow dislocation migration in these alloys, caused by lattice distortion and the presence of B2-ordered precipitates in the SRO state, impedes dislocation motion, prevents the formation of extended semiloops required for the lasso mechanism, and thwarts the coordinated crystal rotations necessary for twinning.
item.limitations: The study uses ideal defect-free crystals with negligible initial dislocation density; the simulation temperature of 10 mK minimizes thermal vibrations but may not reflect behavior at higher temperatures where dislocation avalanches occur; the phase transformation in the SRO sample disappears after unloading, making quantification difficult.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that the absence of twinning in the SRO alloy might change for an alloy with larger B2 precipitates.
quotes: Short-range order—besides making the alloy both stiffer and harder—further increases the size of the plastic zone and the dislocation density there.

The absence of any substantial twinning in the short-range-ordered alloy is plausible as the coordinated crystal rotations required for twinning are thwarted by the breaking of the crystal symmetry caused by the short-range order and the presence of B2 precipitates.

item.research_question: How does short-range order (SRO) and the resulting B2 precipitates affect the mechanical properties, dislocation dynamics, and phase stability of a bcc HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy during nanoindentation compared to a random alloy and pure Ta?
item.material_system: HfNbTaTiZr (bcc high-entropy alloy) with and without short-range order; pure Ta crystal
item.processing_route: Monte Carlo procedure to introduce short-range order; Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations with a volume > 20 million atoms; Nanoindentation simulation
item.test_conditions: Nanoindentation loading and unloading cycles; Pressure range under indenter; Comparison of random vs. SRO alloy vs. pure Ta
key_findings: Short-range order causes a slight stiffening of elastic constants and an increase in indentation hardness on the 10% level.
Dislocation emission from the plastic zone is strongly impeded or absent in the alloys compared to pure Ta.
Dislocation recovery after indenter withdrawal is constrained: the plastic zone radius shrinks by 50% in pure Ta, 30% in the random alloy, and stays approximately constant in the SRO alloy.
Dislocation densities in the plastic zone are highest for the alloys, particularly the SRO alloy.
Twinning is strongest in the random alloy but shrinks to one third of its volume after unloading.
No twinning is found in the SRO alloy; instead, a limited transition to the hcp phase occurs next to the indenter.
HfTi-rich precipitates in the B2 structure impede dislocation motion and contribute to hardening.
item.mechanism: The generation of HfTi-rich precipitates in the B2 structure impedes dislocation motion and helps hardening. The breaking of crystal symmetry and presence of B2 precipitates in the SRO alloy prevent the coordinated motion necessary for twin formation, favoring a limited transition to the hcp phase. Dislocation mobility is decreased in the alloys, leading to constrained recovery and higher dislocation densities.
item.limitations: The text notes that distinguishing a distorted omega phase from a distorted bcc phase is difficult, and that Common Neighbor Analysis (CNA) can misidentify phases under inhomogeneous strain.
item.future_work: Detailed understanding of plasticity might allow design of future alloys with improved performance.
quotes: Short-range order was introduced into the sample by a Monte Carlo procedure.
These changes are caused by the generation of HfTi-rich precipitates in the B2 structure which impede dislocation motion and help hardening.
In that alloy, the breaking of the crystal symmetry and in particular the presence of B2 precipitates prevent the coordinated motion necessary for twin formation
